TI.P:
delivered in Case 9/86
Language of the Case: French.

NP.TXT: Council Directive 80/1263 of 4 December 1980 (Official Journal 1980, L 375, p. 1), which was adopted on the basis of Article 75 (1) (c) of the EEC Treaty, introduces a Community model for the national driving licence, regulates the reciprocal recognition and exchange of national driving licences and initiates the first stage of harmonization of the rules on the issue and validity of driving licences.

QUOT.S.P: After consulting the Commission, Member States shall, in good time and at the latest by 30 June 1982, adopt the laws, regulations or administrative provisions necessary for the implementation of this directive from 1 January 1983.

NP.P: The directive was duly notified to the Kingdom of Belgium.

NP.TXT: Since it had received no notification of definitive measures for implementing the directive and being of the opinion that at that stage the Belgian legislation did not comply with its provisions, the Commission initiated by letter dated 12 March 1984 the procedure provided for in Article 169 of the Treaty by calling on the Belgian Government to submit its observations within a period of two months.

By letter dated 6 July 1984 the Belgian Permanent Representation at the Communities informed the Commission of the state of progress in the adoption of a draft royal decree as amended on the basis of observations made by the Commission and intended to introduce the provisions of the directive into Belgian law. It added that certain provisions provided for by the directive were already applied in Belgian law.

Since the draft was not adopted, the Commission delivered to the Belgian Government on 2 July 1985 the reasoned opinion provided for in the first paragraph of Article 169 of the Treaty and requested it to adopt the measures to comply therewith within a period of two months.

By letter dated 25 September 1985 from the Permanent Representation of Belgium, the Belgian Government acknowledged that it had not satisfied all the obligations imposed on it by the directive but stressed that since the preparatory measures had been taken for the purpose of making Belgian law comply in all respects with the directive, the Belgian authorities were determined to do all in their power to implement the directive speedily. The Permanent Representation of Belgium stated that the Belgian legislation already satisfied the requirements of the directive in a number of fundamental respects.
By application lodged at the Court Registry on 15 January 1986 the Commission brought the present action.
Upon hearing the report of the Judge-Rapporteur and the views of the Advocate General the Court decided to open the oral procedure without any preparatory inquiry.
The Commission claims that the Court should:

Declare that by failing to adopt within the prescribed period the laws, regulations or administrative provisions necessary in order to comply with Council Directive 80/1263 of 4 December 1980 on the introduction of a Community driving licence the Kingdom of Belgium has failed to fulfil its obligations under the EEC Treaty;
Order the Kingdom of Belgium to pay the costs.
The Belgian Government did not expressly formulate any conclusions.
Submissions and arguments of the parties

The Commission states in its application that the current Belgian legislation does not adequately ensure the correct and full application of the directive, especially as regards Article 6 (1) (a) according to which a driving licence may be issued only to those applicants who have passed the practical and theoretical tests and who meet medical standards, the minimum requirements of which may not be substantially less stringent than those set out in Annexes II (as regards the tests) and III (as regards the medical standards).
NP.P: The Commission observes that it is not disputed that the Kingdom of Belgium, contrary to its obligations under the third paragraph of Article 189 and the first paragraph of Article 5 of the Treaty, has not adopted the measures needed to transpose the directive fully into national law within the period prescribed by Article 12 (1) of the directive.

In its reply the Commission takes note of the entry into force of the Royal Decree of 8 October 1985 transposing the provisions of Article 8 of the directive into Belgian law. The royal decree does not however affect the findings on which the Commission's complaints are based.

NP.TXT: The Belgian Government makes known its intention to comply in all respects and as soon as possible with all the provisions of the directive and states that final approval of the draft royal decree intended to adapt the Belgian legislation in its entirety has been delayed by a difficulty in relation to certain procedures concerning medical standards. However, since that difficulty has been resolved and there remain only certain points of detail to be settled, it is envisaged that the legislation will enter into force in its entirety at the end of 1986.
NP.P: The Belgian Government states that the Belgian legislation was partially adapted by the Royal Decree of 8 October 1985 which entered into force on 1 November 1985; it introduced the provisions of Article 8 of the directive into Belgian law and ensures the validity for a certain period of driving licences issued in another Member State to persons who take up residence in Belgium.
